title: Vitamin D supplements and prevention of cancer and cardiovascular disease
authors: Manson JE, Cook NR, Lee IM, Christen W, Bassuk SS, Mora S, et al.
population: US men aged 50 years or older and women aged 55 years or older without cancer or cardiovascular disease, including 5106 African Americans
funder: NIH grants U01 CA138962 and R01 CA138962, with support from the National Cancer Institute, National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute, Office of Dietary Supplements, National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke and National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health. The NIH sponsors had a collaborative role in design, conduct and interpretation; final decisions, data collection, management, analysis, review and approval of the manuscript and the decision to submit rested with the investigators.
inKindSupport: Pharmavite LLC donated vitamin D3, matching placebo and calendar packaging; Pronova BioPharma and BASF donated Omacor fish oil; Quest Diagnostics measured serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D at no cost.
authorConflicts: ICMJE disclosure forms submitted; not itemised in the PMC author manuscript.
result: Vitamin D3 2000 IU per day versus placebo: invasive cancer in 793 of 12,927 versus 824 of 12,944 (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.88 to 1.06); major cardiovascular events in 396 versus 409 (HR 0.97, 0.85 to 1.12); median 5.3 years.
